about.title: Lake Elsinore Product Liability Claims
about.longDescription: Defective products don't just fail in factories — they fail in garages off Riverside Drive, in vehicles merging onto I-15, and in kitchens throughout Lake Elsinore neighborhoods. Whether it's a faulty auto part that contributed to a crash near one of the city's busier corridors, a malfunctioning appliance, or a tool that broke during ordinary use, the resulting injuries can be serious and costly. California law generally allows injured people to pursue a claim under strict liability, meaning you may not need to prove the manufacturer was careless — only that the product was defective and that the defect caused harm. LawProactive helps Lake Elsinore residents connect with an independent attorney familiar with these claims, at no upfront cost. If you were hurt by a product you believed was safe, it's worth having someone review what happened and explain your options before evidence disappears or the product is discarded.

whyChoose.title: Why Lake Elsinore Residents Turn to LawProactive

items.title: Strict Liability Can Simplify Your Case
items.desc: California often doesn't require proof of a manufacturer's negligence — just that the product was defective and caused your injury. This can make it easier to pursue accountability.

items.title: Multiple Parties May Share Responsibility
items.desc: Manufacturers, distributors, and retailers can all potentially be held liable, giving Lake Elsinore claimants more than one avenue to seek recovery.

items.title: Preserving the Product Matters
items.desc: Keeping the defective item intact — rather than discarding or repairing it — can be critical to proving what went wrong, and an attorney can advise on how to protect that evidence.

items.question: Do I need to prove the manufacturer was negligent?
items.answer: Generally, no. California product liability law often allows claims under a strict liability theory, meaning you typically need to show the product was defective and that the defect caused your injury, not that anyone acted carelessly. An independent attorney can review your specific situation to explain how this applies.

items.question: What should I do with the defective product after I'm hurt?
items.answer: Try to preserve it exactly as it was when the injury occurred — don't repair, discard, or heavily clean it. The product itself is often the most important piece of evidence in these claims, and an attorney can advise on safe storage until it's evaluated.

items.question: I was hurt by a car part that failed near Railroad Canyon Road — is that a product liability claim?
items.answer: It could be. If a vehicle component like a tire, brake, or airbag malfunctioned and contributed to a crash on corridors like Railroad Canyon Road or I-15, that may point to a defect claim rather than, or in addition to, a standard crash claim. An attorney can help determine which parties may be responsible.

items.question: Is there a cost to talk to an attorney through LawProactive?
items.answer: No. LawProactive is a free service, and attorneys in our network typically work on contingency, meaning there's no fee unless you recover compensation. There's no obligation to move forward after speaking with someone.
